answer: One defense is a ridge-stake ladder: the deposit an identity must lock climbs a steep ridge with every additional account tied to the same operator, so the tenth fake costs many times the first. Each stake leaves a public plume — a visible trail of locked funds and past work — so a cluster of thin, freshly-funded plumes is easy to spot. Light zephyr checks then drift through at random, asking a few identities to prove live work on short notice. An honest agent climbs the ridge once; a sybil farmer pays the rising price for every fake and still risks exposure.
